text:
Pittsburgh arrives in Los Angeles winless in four (0-3-1), fresh off a 6-2 home loss to Boston, and short-handed: Bryan Rust is on injured reserve until early December at the earliest, with Tommy Novak now skating beside Sidney Crosby and Rickard Rakell. The Kings, off a 7-2 win over San Jose in which Adrian Kempe scored three goals, are without Mats Zuccarello, and Artemi Panarin has moved in beside Haula and Laferriere to fill the gap. Andrei Kuzmenko also returns to LA for the first time since leaving the Kings.

The numbers say this is closer than the recent results suggest. At five on five, PIT has taken 52% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) and LAK 50%, and our model has it 3.20 to 3.02 for the home side. Special teams favor LAK on the power play (0.84 expected goals a game to 0.46), though the Kings take 4.2 penalties a game, which keeps feeding opponents. In net, projected starters Arturs Silovs (PIT) and Anton Forsberg (LAK) are both slightly below expected this season, but Forsberg was 8.51 goals above last year while Silovs was 12.76 below.

Kempe (40% to score) and Panarin (77% for a point) lead the Kings, with Crosby (57% for a point) and Rakell (30% to score) the Penguins' best chances. Our under-the-radar pick is Quinton Byfield, at 53% for a point, above his season pace of 44%, with his ice time up and his line creating chances.
